Definition: from G3106; beatification, i.e. attribution of good fortune:--blessedness.
BiblicalUsage: Makarismos is blessedness, the state of being counted blessed, and Paul uses it to ask who the blessing belongs to. Romans 4:6 says David describeth the blessedness of the man unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works, and Romans 4:9 asks whether this blessedness comes upon the circumcision only or upon the uncircumcision also. Galatians 4:15 asks the Galatians where their blessedness has gone, the joy they once had when they would have plucked out their own eyes for Paul.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Romans 4:9 is the whole argument in one question: if blessedness is for the uncircumcised too, then it is by faith and not by the rite. My position is that Galatians 4:15 is the warning that goes with it, because blessedness can be lost when a church trades faith for rules.
